summary: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that still acts like that element — a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by shells of electrons. Everything is built from atoms.

compareCandidate.label: Atom vs. element
compareCandidate.description: An atom is the smallest particle of a substance that is still that substance — a single, indivisible-in-chemistry unit. An element is a large quantity of identical atoms — a pure substance made of only one kind of atom. One atom is one brick; the element is the whole wall.

processes: Being the smallest unit that keeps an element's identity
Building molecules, compounds, and everything else
Sitting as the foundation of all matter
plainLanguageExplanation: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that is still that element. Everything around you — the air, the water, your body, your phone — is built from atoms, the tiny bricks of matter. Inside an atom there are three kinds of particles: protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral), packed together in the nucleus at the center, and electrons (negative), orbiting far outside in shells. Here is the surprising part: atoms are mostly empty space. If an atom were a stadium, the nucleus would be a marble at the center spot and the electrons would be tiny specks circling in the upper seats — with empty air between. Yet those empty atoms, stacked together, make up everything solid in the universe. There are about 90 naturally occurring kinds of atoms — the elements — and every combination of them builds every substance that exists. Atoms are the alphabet of the universe: a few dozen letters, endless words.

whyItMatters: Atoms are the fundamental building blocks of all matter. Understanding the atom — its nucleus, its electron shells, and its mostly-empty structure — is the foundation of every idea in chemistry: elements, molecules, bonds, and reactions. Everything begins with the atom.
didYouKnow: A single drop of water contains about 1.6 sextillion (1.6 × 10²¹) atoms — far more than all the grains of sand on every beach on Earth.
compareReason: The atom-element relationship (one particle versus the whole substance) is the foundation of all matter — comparing them shows how a single brick builds an entire wall.
